context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor in AWS (eu-west-1) and provides case management for fraud analysts. It satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS within a €25,000 monthly budget.

## Key Elements
* **Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System** (Software System)
* **Payment Gateway / Acquirer** (External System)
* **Fraud Analyst** (Person)
* **Card Networks & Tokenization Vault** (External System)
* **Core-Banking / Ledger System** (External System)
* **Model Training Environment** (External System)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway -> Fraud System via **gRPC over HTTP/2** for real-time scoring
* Fraud Analyst -> Fraud System via **HTTPS** with **MFA and RBAC**
* Fraud System -> Tokenization Vault via **mTLS / HTTPS** for token resolution
* Fraud System -> Core-Banking System via **HTTPS / REST** for transaction disposition
* Model Training Environment -> Fraud System via secure model artifact ingestion using **AWS Signer / KMS** cryptographic verification

## Technology Stack
* **AWS Fargate / ECS or Serverless Containers**: Selected for managed infrastructure, minimizing operational overhead for a 3-engineer team within the €25k budget.
* **AWS S3 Object Lock**: Utilized for Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) storage to enforce tamper-evident, 7-year auditability (R-06).
* **AWS KMS / Signer**: Implemented for cryptographic signature verification of hot-reloaded model artifacts and data encryption.
* **gRPC / HTTP/2**: Chosen for machine-to-machine communication to guarantee P99 latency below 50ms at 3,000 TPS.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages managed AWS services to fit the operational capacity of a 3-engineer team and the €25,000 monthly budget. Strict trust boundaries, cryptographic controls, and WORM storage ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and auditable 7-year retention.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and routes suspicious cases to analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS compliance, <50ms P99 latency, and auditable decision logging within budget.

## Key Elements
- **API Gateway & Routing Layer**: AWS API Gateway and ALB handling ingress and tokenization hand-offs.
- **Real-Time Scoring Service**: Go container on Amazon ECS on EC2 processing synchronous authorizations via gRPC.
- **Case Management Backend**: Java Spring Boot container on Amazon ECS on Fargate managing analyst review workflows.
- **Data & Audit Stores**: Amazon DynamoDB (with AWS KMS and DynamoDB Streams) for tamper-evident audit logs and feature store; Amazon RDS PostgreSQL for case management.
- **Messaging & Eventing**: Amazon SQS, SNS, and EventBridge decoupling real-time scoring from asynchronous auditing and case creation.

## Relationships
- **Payment Gateway to API Gateway**: Ingests authorization requests over HTTPS.
- **API Gateway to Real-Time Scoring Service**: Forwards requests using gRPC for low-latency evaluation.
- **Real-Time Scoring Service to DynamoDB**: Writes cryptographically hashed, immutable decision payloads via AWS KMS.
- **Real-Time Scoring Service to SQS**: Asynchronously publishes review cases and audit events.
- **SQS to Case Management Backend**: Triggers analyst workflows for suspicious transactions.

## Technology Stack
- **Go**: Used for the Real-Time Scoring Service to guarantee P99 latency below 50ms at 3,000 TPS.
- **Amazon ECS on EC2**: Provides predictable CPU pinning and avoids cold-start virtualization overhead for the hot path.
- **Amazon ECS on Fargate**: Runs the async Case Management Backend to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
- **Amazon DynamoDB & AWS KMS**: Delivers low-latency storage with cryptographic hashing and WORM backups for 7-year tamper-evident auditability.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Eliminates static secrets by injecting credentials dynamically at runtime.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go on ECS EC2 for predictable, ultra-low latency transaction screening while leveraging serverless queues and Fargate for cost-effective case management. Strict separation of concerns, in-memory PAN handling, and cryptographic audit logging fulfill PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit requirements within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.

API Gateway & Routing Layer.analysis:
## Overview
This system screens real-time payment authorizations for fraud to protect a mid-size payment processor. It evaluates requests for approval, decline, or manual review while providing case management for analysts.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- Card Networks & Tokenization Vault
- API Gateway & Routing Layer (AWS ALB + AWS WAF, Go Routing & Tokenization Proxy)
- Real-Time Scoring Service (Go container on Amazon ECS on EC2)
- Case Management Backend (Java Spring Boot container on Amazon ECS on Fargate)
- Data & Audit Stores (Amazon DynamoDB with AWS KMS, DynamoDB Streams, Amazon RDS PostgreSQL)
- Messaging & Eventing (Amazon SQS, SNS, Amazon EventBridge)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> API Gateway & Routing Layer: Ingests authorization requests over HTTPS with mTLS and JWT [mTLS / HTTPS]
- API Gateway & Routing Layer -> Card Networks & Tokenization Vault: Resolves PAN to token [mTLS / HTTPS]
- API Gateway & Routing Layer -> Real-Time Scoring Service: Forwards scrubbed payloads for low-latency evaluation [gRPC over HTTP/2]
- Real-Time Scoring Service -> Data & Audit Stores: Persists audit logs and retrieves models [TLS / TCP]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ALB & AWS WAF: Edge termination and WAF filtering to meet P99 latency targets within budget.
- Go: Used for the Routing & Tokenization Proxy and Real-Time Scoring Service for minimal resource footprint and high performance.
- Java Spring Boot: Used for Case Management Backend.
- Amazon DynamoDB & RDS PostgreSQL: Persistent storage with AWS KMS encryption for tamper-evident audit trails.
- AWS Secrets Manager: Secure credential injection with automatic rotation.

## Rationale
The architecture uses AWS managed services and Go-based microservices to comfortably achieve the sub-50ms P99 latency requirement while strictly adhering to PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. This lean design operates efficiently within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and supports management by a three-engineer team.

Real-Time Scoring Service.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations, ensuring secure evaluation, compliance, and case management for financial analysts. It processes high-throughput transactions while maintaining strict auditability and low-latency availability.

## Key Elements
- API Handler Component (Go `net/http` + `grpc`)
- Token Resolution Client Component (Go `net/http`)
- Feature Store Cache Component (Embedded Go LRU Cache / Redis Client)
- Scoring Engine Component (Go WebAssembly / ONNX runtime)
- Audit & Event Dispatcher Component (Go AWS SDK)
- Circuit Breaker / Fallback Component (Go `gobreaker`)

## Relationships
- API Gateway & Routing Layer -> API Handler Component: Forwards low-latency evaluation requests [gRPC]
- Token Resolution Client Component -> Card Networks & Tokenization Vault: Fetches tokenized attributes [mTLS / HTTPS]
- Audit & Event Dispatcher Component -> Amazon DynamoDB: Writes immutable decision payloads and audit logs [AWS KMS / DynamoDB API]
- Scoring Engine Component -> Model Training Environment: Ingests signed model artifacts [AWS Signer / KMS]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency execution fitting the 50ms P99 requirement.
- Amazon ECS on EC2: Provides predictable CPU performance and cost control within the 25,000 EUR/month budget.
- ONNX Runtime: Executes lightweight machine learning models in-memory without Python runtime overhead.
- AWS KMS: Secures encryption keys, token data, and cryptographic audit signature chains.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go microservices deployed on Amazon ECS on EC2 to guarantee the required 50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS. Integrated cryptographic controls and immutable audit trails satisfy strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability mandates within budget.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Backend manages analyst review workflows and fraud cases for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system. It operates on AWS ECS Fargate, providing secure, auditable case resolution while ensuring PCI-DSS compliance and strict data masking.

## Key Elements
- Workflow Engine Component (Spring State Machine)
- Analyst Portal API Controller (Spring MVC/REST)
- Case Repository Layer (Spring Data JPA)
- Tokenization & Masking Service Client (Spring Cloud OpenFeign with Resilience4j)

## Relationships
- Analyst Portal API Controller -> Workflow Engine Component: Invokes via direct method calls
- Analyst Portal API Controller -> Case Repository Layer: Persists and retrieves state via Amazon RDS PostgreSQL
- Workflow Engine Component -> Case Repository Layer: Persists state using optimistic locking via Amazon RDS PostgreSQL
- Analyst Portal API Controller -> Tokenization & Masking Service Client: Retrieves masked payload data for rendering case details
- Tokenization & Masking Service Client -> Card Networks & Tokenization Vault: Fetches tokenized card data via mTLS and IAM authentication

## Technology Stack
- Java Spring Boot: Core framework chosen for enterprise reliability and rapid feature delivery by a 3-engineer team.
- Amazon ECS on Fargate: Container runtime selected to eliminate OS-level patching overhead and maintain PCI-DSS compliance.
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Relational database utilizing Row-Level Security and encryption for tamper-evident audit trails.
- Resilience4j: Fault-tolerance library used in the Feign client to ensure fail-fast resilience during external vault degradation.
- AWS Secrets Manager: Used for runtime credential injection via IAM task roles.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict PCI-DSS security constraints and 7-year auditability with the operational limitations of a 3-engineer team through managed AWS services. Containerizing on Fargate and leveraging robust Spring components ensures high availability, strict data isolation, and a predictable cost structure within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Overview
[The Data & Audit Stores container provides secure, low-latency feature storage, relational case management, and tamper-evident 7-year audit logging for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system on AWS.]

## Key Elements
* Audit & Decision Log Store (Amazon DynamoDB with AWS KMS and DynamoDB Streams)
* Feature Store (Amazon DynamoDB)
* Case Management Database (Amazon RDS PostgreSQL)
* Audit Archival Worker (AWS Lambda)
* Long-Term Audit Archive (Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval with S3 Object Lock)

## Relationships
* Real-Time Scoring Service -> Feature Store: Read/write fraud features via DynamoDB SDK (HTTPS/TLS 1.3)
* Real-Time Scoring Service -> Audit & Decision Log Store: Appends immutable decision records via DynamoDB API (HTTPS/TLS 1.3)
* Case Management Backend <-> Case Management DB: Relational data persistence via PostgreSQL JDBC (TLS 1.3)
* Audit & Decision Log Store -> Audit Archival Worker: Streams change records via DynamoDB Streams (Internal AWS Event Source)
* Audit Archival Worker -> Long-Term Audit Archive: Writes tamper-evident archives via S3 API (HTTPS/TLS 1.3)

## Technology Stack
* Amazon DynamoDB: Selected for feature and audit storage to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency.
* Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Selected for case management to handle complex relational analyst workflows.
* Amazon S3 Glacier: Selected for 7-year audit retention with S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode) to meet budget and compliance constraints.
* AWS Lambda: Selected for serverless audit stream processing with minimal operational overhead.
* AWS KMS: Selected for customer-managed encryption keys to ensure strict data protection.

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and sub-50ms latency requirements through isolated AWS data stores and managed services. It respects a €25,000 monthly budget and a 3-engineer team constraint by leveraging serverless archival pipelines.]

Messaging & Eventing.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst review workflows. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Service (Go container on Amazon ECS on EC2)
- Case Management Backend (Java Spring Boot container on Amazon ECS on Fargate)
- Audit Event Publisher (Lightweight Go client with asynchronous batching)
- Case Queue (Amazon SQS FIFO Queue with content-based deduplication and DLQ)
- Model Event Bus (Amazon EventBridge)
- Audit SNS Topic (Amazon SNS with fan-out pattern)

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Service -> Audit Event Publisher: In-process function call, publishing asynchronously via AWS SDK over HTTPS [TLS 1.3]
- Audit Event Publisher -> Audit SNS Topic: Publishes audit logs [HTTPS, AWS KMS CMK encryption]
- Real-Time Scoring Service -> Case Queue: Sends review cases for suspicious transactions [Amazon SQS FIFO API, HTTPS, AWS KMS CMK encryption]
- Case Queue -> Case Management Backend: Long-polling for review workflows [AWS SDK, HTTPS]
- Model Event Bus -> Real-Time Scoring Service: Broadcasts model hot-reloading signals [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon SQS FIFO: Ensures strict message ordering per account to prevent analyst review race conditions.
- Amazon SNS & EventBridge: Provides reliable fan-out and event broadcasting with minimal operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
- AWS KMS: Secures all queues, topics, and event buses with Customer Managed Keys for PCI-DSS compliance.
- Fluent Bit & LUKS: Encrypts ephemeral local disk-spill buffers for circuit breaker recovery.
- AWS X-Ray & CloudWatch: Enforces distributed tracing and metric alarms to meet the 1-minute fallback availability threshold.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages managed AWS messaging services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while meeting strict sub-50ms latency constraints. It enforces robust security, encryption, and FIFO ordering to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability mandates within budget.
